macro.event: FHFA House Price Index (Jun and Q2)
macro.note: FHFA-confirmed, 9:00 AM on the agency's own release schedule. May ran +0.3% month over month and +2.2% year over year. The Case-Shiller June read is expected the same hour on cadence, but S&P publishes no forward schedule page so that one is NOT date-verified

Conference Board-confirmed for the last Tuesday of the month at 10:00. July was 90.8, down 1.4 points from an upwardly revised 92.2, with present situation 114.9 and expectations 74.7. The cross-check on Michigan's collapse to 51.0 preliminary. No credible non-aggregator consensus exists, so none is shown
Census and HUD-confirmed. June ran 628,000 annualised with 9.3 months of supply and a $398,300 median price. The most rate-sensitive number on the board with the 10Y at 4.67% and the 30Y above 5.2%
Richmond Fed-confirmed, released between 10:00 and 10:10. A regional read into next week's ISM

Size, date and CUSIP 91282CRH6 from Treasury's own 8/20 offering announcement; settles 8/31. First of three coupon auctions this week. A $95B 42-day bill also goes at 11:30. Note for the record: aggregator sites are already displaying a 4.315% actual for today's 2-year - that number does not exist yet and must not be used
BEA-confirmed for WEDNESDAY. June was +3.7% headline and +3.3% core year over year, with the saving rate at 2.7%. The single biggest input to September hike odds, and it lands the same day as Nvidia

macro.event: GDP Q2 second estimate and Durable Goods (Jul)
macro.note: BEA- and Census-confirmed. Advance Q2 real GDP was +1.5% annualised against +2.1% in Q1; June durable orders were +0.3%. Treasury also sells $70B of 5-year at 1:00 PM and reopens a $28B FRN at 11:30

Prior 206,000, down 6,000, with the four-week average at 204,000 - still near cycle lows. Advance goods trade at 8:30 (June deficit $101.5B), KC Fed manufacturing at 11:00, and the $44B 7-year auction at 1:00

Kansas City Fed, theme Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy. The Board's own August calendar lists only three speeches all month - Cook on the 5th, Bowman on the 8th and Warsh on the 28th - so there is no Fed speaker at all before Friday and the Committee speaks with one voice

macro.event: Fed Chair Warsh keynote at Jackson Hole
macro.note: His first as Chair, 10:00 AM on the Fed's own calendar. Michigan final sentiment (prelim 51.0) and the BLS preliminary payroll benchmark revision both land at 10:00 the same morning, which makes Friday the densest hour of the week
